$comment: Golden vectors for ONE question: is this folder spelled for the OTHER operating system — a root the
server on this side must skip rather than refuse?
VS Code user settings are shared between a WSL window and a plain Windows window on one machine, so a
question-consultant disk root written from WSL (`/home/jinx/git`) is read by the Windows window too. Each
side runs its own coai-mcp. The Windows server refused that root as 'not a directory on this machine' and
the panel raised a failure toast on every start (operator, 2026-10-09, extension 0.65.0 / coai-mcp 0.44.2).
The root is not wrong — it is the other side's folder, and the server THERE reads it.
Both halves decide this independently — `QuestionRoots.OtherSide` in C#
(src_mcp/src/Server/QuestionConsult/QuestionConsultSettings.cs) for what the server skips, and
`spelledForTheOtherOs` in the extension (src_vs_code/src/pathFamily.ts) for what the Settings page says
beside a stored root. Two self-consistent loaders cannot notice they disagree, so both suites answer this
file (QuestionConsultSettingsTests.cs, pathFamily.test.ts).
`vectors` is the SPELLING alone: `onWindows` is the verdict of a server or window running on Windows,
`elsewhere` of one on Linux, WSL or macOS. A root that is neither side's absolute spelling (relative,
drive-relative) is the same side's, and is refused there by name as before.
`existence` is the DECISION, and the spelling is not enough for it (the plan round, 2026-10-09): on Windows
`/work` is a legal root-relative path to the folder `work`. So a root spelled for the other OS is the other
side's only when it is NOT an existing directory on this machine; one that exists here is this side's and goes
through the ordinary checks. Answered by `QuestionRoots.OtherSideHere` and the extension's `otherSideHere`.
`resolution` is WHERE such a root is looked for (the code round, 2026-10-09). A root-relative Windows path names
the current drive, and the extension host and coai-mcp need not stand on the same one — so both halves qualify
it with the SYSTEM drive (`%SystemDrive%`, `C:` when unset): on Windows a root with one leading `/`, or a `\`
not followed by another, becomes `<drive>` + the path with backslashes, for the existence decision AND, on the
server, for the root it keeps. Everything else, and every root elsewhere, is unchanged (trimmed). Answered by
`QuestionRoots.Qualified` and the extension's `qualified`.
`executable` is a CLI path — a reviewer's, a consultant's, a question row's or a chat model's `executablePath`
(todo/PLAN_paths_per_side.md E1.2). The roots' rule, for a FILE: one spelled for the other operating system is
skipped — the CLI is looked up on PATH by its runtime's name, never launched, never refused — ONLY when the disk
confirms no such file here (`existsHere` false and no `unknownHere`). On Windows `/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe` is a
legal root-relative path: it is looked for qualified with `systemDrive` and, when there or when the disk cannot
tell, runs qualified (the cadence consultant, E1). `here` is what this side runs (empty = the PATH lookup) and
`otherSide` whether the value was skipped; `windows` is the side asking. Answered by the extension's
`pathForThisSide` (what it writes into COAI_VENDORS and
what it launches) and by coai-mcp's `ExecutablePaths.Here` (its own vendor read, for a settings file an older
extension wrote).
